references.text: Moses' answer to Pharaoh where he confirms that he will not see his face again
Moses leaves Pharaoh in anger after this confrontation
Pharaoh calls Moses back after the tenth plague, despite his threat
Absalom was not allowed to see the king's face as a sign of disfavor, parallel to being banished from a ruler's presence
Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two years without seeing the king's face, illustrating the seriousness of being denied access
Joseph warned his brothers not to see his face without Benjamin, a similar warning about appearing before a ruler's presence
Both verses confirm the theological principle that no human can see God's face and live.
Both verses illustrate the dangers of approaching God's presence without proper consecration.
Both verses use the expression 'send away from my face' to illustrate God's judgment and rejection.
